requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
**Implementation.** The skill file `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` is the implementation. It is marked with an `:impl:` anchor on `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill` in `md/requirements/cli.md`. Each obligation in the requirement text is covered:

- **Read code and tests.** The opening paragraph tells the agent to read existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation and tests. It also says to follow behavior through the code and not rely only on test names or top-level dispatch.
- **Map every first-party test.** The first inventory covers every first-party runnable test or case, including integration tests, doctests and parameterized cases. The skill tells the agent to put at least one `{test}` reference with a full requirement or example name on each test definition or case. It also forbids using a file-level tag in place of per-test references.
- **Map every source unit implementing end-user-visible behavior.** The second inventory covers every explicit Rust function or method, including helpers. It also covers public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors and distinct observable branches, and it says a tagged entry point does not cover deeper code. Each inventoried item must get a reference chosen by the reference procedure. That procedure ends in `habeas:none`, which may not be used for end-user-observable behavior that no requirement specifies.
- **Report gaps and require independent review.** The skill says to have both inventories independently reviewed against the source and tests before claiming complete coverage. It says to claim 100% only when neither inventory has unmapped items. It says to list remaining gaps with locations and reasons, and not to invent evidence or silently exclude difficult cases.
- **Bundled.** `Cargo.toml` publishes `assets/skills` through the Symposium metadata. The test checks this.

The skill also contains other guidance: user review of inferred requirements, the flip and rewording guidance, authoring-harness use, and the reference procedure. Other requirements specify that guidance and carry `:impl:` anchors to the same file, so it is not unspecified behavior. Those requirements are `requirements_review_skill`, `behavior_review_guidance`, `internal_detail_guidance`, `flip_guidance` and `authoring.batch`.

**Tests.** `bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories` in `tests/authoring_cli.rs` carries `{test}` for this requirement. The helpers `bundled_skill` and `assert_phrases` also carry `{test}` for it. The test does four things:

- It checks that the Cargo manifest publishes `assets/skills`.
- It checks the skill's frontmatter name and description.
- It uses `include_str!`, so a missing skill file would fail the build.
- It asserts the key directive phrases for each obligation: reading code and tests, the test inventory and `{test}` tagging, the function inventory and per-function references, independent review before claiming completeness, the 100% rule, and listing gaps.

For a documentation-style requirement, phrase-presence testing is the practical way to verify content. Failure cases are covered in that dropping any directive phrase fails the test. Sibling tests also check the shared parts of the skill.

I found no unmarked implementation and no unspecified behavior outside the covered requirements.
